cd /tmp; kubectl get endpoints -n test-social-network | awk '$2=="<none>"'; kubectl get svc -n test-social-network -o json | jq -r '.items[]|"\(.metadata.name) \(.spec.ports[0].port) \(.spec.ports[0].targetPort)"' | awk '$2!=$3'; kubectl get deploy -n test-social-network -o json | jq -r '.items[]|"\(.metadata.name) \(.spec.template.spec.containers[0].ports[0].containerPort)"' | grep -v -E ' (9090|6379|11211|27017)$'; for p in $(kubectl get pods -n test-social-network -o name); do echo "== $p"; kubectl logs -n test-social-network $p --tail=3 2>&1 | grep -i -E "error|fail|exception"; done

cd /tmp; kubectl get svc,deploy -n test-social-network -o yaml | grep -E "^    name:|port:|targetPort|containerPort" | paste -sd' ' | sed 's/    name:/\n/g' | grep -i post-storage; kubectl logs -n test-social-network deploy/post-storage-service --tail=5; kubectl get endpoints post-storage-service -n test-social-network

kubectl patch svc post-storage-service -n test-social-network --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/ports/0/targetPort","value":9090}]'; sleep 3; kubectl get endpoints post-storage-service -n test-social-network
agent.summary:
The anomaly was a wrong port on the `post-storage-service` Service, and I've fixed it. I didn't send a test request through the app afterwards, so the fix is confirmed only by the endpoint change.

**What I found:** The Service had `targetPort: 9999`, but the pod listens on 9090. As a result, `compose-post-service` logged "Failed to connect post-storage-client", and `nginx-thrift` returned "Connection refused" on post-compose requests.

**What I changed:** I patched the Service's `targetPort` to 9090. Its endpoint now points to `10.244.1.209:9090`.

**Not changed:** `user-service` and `user-timeline-service` logged MongoDB connection errors at startup. I read these as startup noise because the pods are Running, and I didn't check them further.
